title: Stop Posting AI-Generated Videos and Calling Them Game Development
author: Difficult_Tip_9307
selftext:
I'm posting this on behalf of a friend who doesn't have a Reddit account. He specifically asked me to share this message.



My friend has been struggling with AI-assisted game development for the past two months.



Two months of broken code, endless bugs, systems that don't work together, and AI assistants repeatedly failing to deliver what they claim they can build.



Then he comes across this community and sees all these spectacular videos supposedly showcasing AI-developed games.



But here's the question: are we actually looking at real games, or just AI-generated videos?



Anyone can generate an impressive cinematic video with AI. That doesn't mean they've developed a game.



If you've actually built something using AI, then show it running inside a real game engine.



Show us Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, or whatever engine you're using. Show the actual scene, the editor, the camera moving through the environment, and the game running in real time.



Not another polished cinematic video. Not another AI-generated animation pretending to be gameplay.



We're not asking for your source code. We're not asking you to release your project.



We're asking for something incredibly simple:



Show actual footage from the game engine.



If your game is real, demonstrating it running in the engine shouldn't be an unreasonable request.



My friend has spent two months dealing with the reality of AI game development, and he's tired of seeing videos that make it look like anyone can create an incredible game with a few prompts.



Maybe some of these projects are genuine. Great. Then show the real development process instead of just the final cinematic presentation.



A generated video is not a game. A beautiful animation is not a functioning game engine. And impressive visuals are not proof of actual development.



AI game development needs more transparency and fewer misleading showcases.



Stop showing us what AI can imagine. Start showing us what AI can actually build.
